A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Order-Aware Interactive Segmentation (OIS). Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original OIS evaluations on HQSeg44K and DAVIS, efficiency measurements, component ablations, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds depth-source robustness experiments, further ablations, backbone controls, and COCO+LVIS training results.

M1.justification: The proposed architecture, order-map construction, attention equations, dense/sparse prompt fusion, and training loss remain unchanged. The alternative backbones and module sequences are experimental variants; A.10 tests the object-before-order sequence already depicted in Figure 2 of v1.

E1.justification: A.14 adds OIS training on COCO+LVIS, whereas v1 reports OIS training only on HQSeg44K. This extends training-data coverage within natural-image interactive segmentation; the evaluation datasets remain HQSeg44K and DAVIS.

E2.justification: Corresponding Tables 1–5 retain their comparator membership. New controlled comparisons reuse previously evaluated segmentation methods. DepthAnything V1, ZoeDepth, and MAE are tested as OIS configurations, while the newly cited OACE is not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: A.9–A.14 add substantial controlled evaluation designs: varying depth estimators, reversing attention-module order, separating positive/negative order maps, comparing backbone pretraining with attention removal, and matching training-data sources. The original click simulation, metrics, and main experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's DAVIS component ablations and depth-integration comparison, v3 tests sensitivity to depth sources and prediction errors, large depth variation within targets, module ordering, positive versus negative order maps, and backbone choice. It also adds component ablations on HQSeg44K and training-data controls.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The additional results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their scores, while Tables 6–12 add substantial results under new conditions. For example, COCO+LVIS-trained OIS reports NoC90 of 5.16 on HQSeg44K and 4.41 on DAVIS. Figure 8 also reassigns the first tree example's prediction panels and five-click IoUs from OIS 68/SegNext 80 to OIS 80/SegNext 68, reversing that reported comparison.

T1.justification: The order-map definitions and attention formulations in Equations 1–5 are unchanged. The added appendix sections contain empirical studies and interpretations, without new formal assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same methodological contributions and headline accuracy/efficiency claims, including the 7.61 and 1.32 one-click mIoU advantages. The new appendix experiments support these claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: A.9 newly attributes robustness to erroneous depth maps and large within-object depth variation to object-aware attention. A.12 explains different roles for positive order maps in initial selection and negative order maps in later corrections; A.13 distinguishes attention-module benefits from backbone benefits. The original thin-occluder failure discussion remains.

D1.justification: v3 clarifies that latency includes depth prediction and segmentation, and A.4 explains the retained MM-SAM and DepthEncoder configurations more explicitly. It removes the abstract's project-page link and adds a statement that source code will be released pending approval. The principal hyperparameter and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds a brief related-work discussion of OACE and references for ZoeDepth, DepthAnything V1, MAE, COCO, and LVIS. The existing related-work taxonomy and positioning of the main contributions remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and methodology are nearly verbatim. Changes include local wording edits, a rewritten A.4 explanation, ethics and reproducibility statements, appended sections A.9–A.14, and the conference-publication header, without substantial reorganization of the existing argument.

P2.justification: Tables 6–12 and Figures 15–17 substantially expand the empirical displays with controlled comparisons and paired depth/segmentation visualizations. Figure 6 gains a depth-map column, Figure 8 revises prediction panels and labels, and click-color captions are clarified. Most earlier displays are retained with pagination and placement changes.

improvement.justification: The backbone and training-data controls in A.13–A.14 substantially reduce confounds left by v1's comparisons, while A.9 directly examines dependence on depth quality. These additions strengthen validation of the central method. The removed project link, conditional code release, and reporting errors such as Table 8's incorrect NoC90 delta temper reproducibility and polish, but do not outweigh the stronger experimental support.
